title: oncall: Clipboard artifact collector and hand-off clipper
author: Ava Chang
description:
Motivation: On-call handoffs and postmortems often require curating a small set of diagnostic artifacts (logs, span snippets, config lines, short runbook links) and sharing them with a responder or another team. Current workflows involve manual copy/paste or creating large zip bundles; both are error-prone and leak too much context. This change introduces a lightweight 'Clipboard' concept in incident-bot: an ephemeral, scrubbed artifact collector that responders can build interactively (CLI or Slack modal) and then share as a single short link or attach to an incident. The Clipboard is intentionally compact (metadata + pointers + small text snippets) and enforces automated PII scrubbing and retention/audit rules.

What this PR does: Adds a new Clipboard service (API + DB model), a small frontend in the Slack modal flow, a CLI helper rbx clip to create and share clipboards, and a hand-off clipper command that attaches a Clipboard reference to an incident or creates a one-time share link. Key properties: 1) automated scrubbing pipeline using the existing sanitizer library with additional redaction rules for secrets/tokens; 2) manifest.json describing included artifacts and provenance; 3) configurable retention (default 7 days) and audit logging entries for every create/share action; 4) feature-flag gated rollout and RBAC check to prevent cross-tenant exposure.

Design notes: The Clipboard stores short text blobs (max 64KB each) and pointer references to existing storage artifacts (log slices in telemetry, trace IDs). We chose not to allow arbitrary file uploads to keep the surface area small. The share link is a short, opaque token that maps to the Clipboard ID plus an expiry timestamp. All share actions record an audit entry (user, target incident, timestamp) to support later review. Scrubber runs synchronously on small text blobs and asynchronously validates referenced pointers.

Testing & rollout: Unit tests added for sanitizer rules, manifest generation, and DB model. End-to-end test simulates Slack flow + CLI create + attach to incident. The feature is behind feature flag "oncall_clipboard" and will be enabled for internal SRE org first. We also added a migration to introduce clipboard_table with backward-compatible defaults. The migration is small and reversible.

Operational considerations: retention policy is configurable via env var CLIPBOARD_RETENTION_DAYS. Audit logs are shipped to the existing audit stream so SOC teams already ingest them. We added rate limits to the create endpoint to avoid abuse. A small metrics set was added (clip.create, clip.share, clip.scrub_failures). Rollback plan: turn off feature flag and run cleanup job to expire outstanding clips earlier if necessary.

review_conversation: Samir Patel: Nice, this looks useful. A couple of questions: (1) how do we ensure no large logs leak in pointers? (2) will the scrubber handle stack traces with tokens embedded?

Ava Chang: Replying: (1) pointer references are to internal log slice IDs and we enforce a maximum pointer size and an allowlist of sources; the UI warns users if a pointer refers to a large archive. (2) scrubber has a regex/entropy-based rule we added; see sanitizer/rules/clipboard_rules.py — unit tests cover common stack-trace patterns.
Leah Gomez: Please add an explicit opt-out for copying raw environment variables into a clip (security).
Ava Chang: Added a UI checkbox and server-side check to block env var patterns; updated tests to assert rejection.
Ravi Menon: Can we log the full diff of the manifest on attach for audit? Might increase audit volume but helpful.
Ava Chang: We log a compact manifest summary (counts + hashes) and store the full manifest in the audit S3 bucket; added a note to ops-runbook about retention.
Samir Patel: CI flake in e2e; re-run tests after addressing timing (fixed by adding retry/backoff).
CI Bot: Tests passed after re-run. Approved by Samir and Leah.
merge_outcome: merged via squash with message 'oncall: Clipboard artifact collector and hand-off clipper (feat)'. Release notes added.
release_notes: Add an on-call Clipboard feature: small, scrubbed, shareable collections of diagnostic artifacts; CLI helper rbx clip; Slack modal integration; retention and audit controls. Feature behind 'oncall_clipboard' feature flag; enabled for internal SRE first.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: oncall_clipboard=false by default. Env: CLIPBOARD_RETENTION_DAYS (default 7). Audit stream: clipboard.audit.* metrics. If disabling, run cleanup job: scripts/cleanup/expire_clipboards.py
